definition: The state values available to one particular render of a component. Event handlers created by that render read those values even after requesting a future update.
example: A handler created with count 4 still reads 4 immediately after requesting count 5.

definition: A JavaScript function together with access to the variables from the surrounding scope where it was created. In React, a handler can retain the state values belonging to the render that created it.
example: A delayed Send callback can retain the recipient selected when Send was clicked.

definition: React grouping state updates before updating the displayed interface. Updates made during one event handler can be processed together after that handler finishes.
example: Two setters inside a click handler do not display an intermediate state between the calls.

definition: The ordered pending replacements and updater functions that React processes to calculate the next state. An updater receives the pending result of preceding updates.
example: Replacing with 5 and then incrementing produces 6.

definition: A state updater that only calculates and returns next state from its input. It does not modify existing objects, send requests or write external data.
example: Returning a new task array is pure; pushing into an external log from the updater is not.

definition: A state setter request that supplies the next value directly rather than a function to transform pending state. Later replacements in the same queue can replace earlier pending results.
example: setCount(2) asks for 2 rather than asking React to add 2.

definition: An update that constructs replacement data without changing previously stored objects or arrays. Unchanged objects may be shared when they remain read-only.
example: Changing a nested address creates a new profile and a new address object.

definition: JavaScript syntax written with three dots that expands values into a new array or copies own enumerable properties into an object literal. Object and array copying with spread is shallow.
example: { ...profile, city: "York" } copies profile fields and then overrides city.

definition: A copy of one container level whose nested objects are still shared by reference. Editing a nested shared object changes what both containers can observe.
example: [...tasks] makes a new array, but its task objects remain the same objects.

definition: An object property marked to appear in ordinary property enumeration. Object spread copies the source object’s own enumerable properties, rather than every property reachable through inheritance.
example: Object spread copies ordinary fields such as name and city.

definition: A JavaScript comparison operation React uses to decide whether a proposed state value is unchanged. For objects and arrays, an existing object compared with itself is the same even if its contents were edited.
example: Passing the same mutated object to a setter can lead React to skip the update.

definition: A form input whose current text or selected state is supplied through React props and updated through an event handler. Text uses value; checkboxes use checked.
example: A checkbox renders checked from boolean state and stores event.target.checked in onChange.

definition: A form input whose current value is managed by the browser rather than continuously supplied by React. defaultValue or defaultChecked can specify its initial value.
example: A text field with only defaultValue keeps later edits in the browser.

definition: The value prop supplies a controlled text input’s current string. defaultValue instead supplies the initial value of an uncontrolled text input.
example: Use value={title} when React state should determine every displayed edit.

definition: The checked prop supplies a controlled checkbox’s selected boolean state. defaultChecked supplies the initial selection for an uncontrolled checkbox.
example: A task’s done boolean controls whether its checkbox is selected.

definition: A React input event handled through onChange when the user edits a field. Controlled inputs update their controlling state immediately from the event target.
example: Read event.target.value for text and event.target.checked for a checkbox.

definition: The form action triggered by a submit control or another supported submission method such as keyboard submission. React can handle it through the form’s onSubmit prop.
example: A task form handles Save in onSubmit rather than depending only on a button click.

definition: An event method that cancels a cancelable event’s normal browser action. It does not itself stop the event from travelling to other handlers.
example: Calling preventDefault in onSubmit prevents the form’s usual navigation.

definition: The way an event travels through related elements and their event handlers. Stopping propagation is different from cancelling a default browser action.
example: preventDefault can cancel form navigation while the event still propagates.

definition: A visible name associated with a form control. In JSX, a label can wrap the input or use htmlFor matching the input’s unique id.
example: A visible Task label names the title field.

definition: Moving a shared state value to the closest common parent that needs to coordinate it. The parent passes data and change-request callbacks to children.
example: Two sibling editors display the one text string owned by their parent.

definition: A function supplied as a component prop so the child can report an event or request a change from its parent. Its arguments are part of the component’s design.
example: An Editor calls onChange with the next string rather than editing the value prop.

definition: A component whose important information is supplied through props by its parent. It may still have independent local state for other details.
example: An Editor receives text and a change callback while keeping a help-panel toggle locally.

definition: Information that can be calculated from current props or existing state. Usually calculate it during render rather than storing and synchronising another copy.
example: Filter tasks from tasks and query; calculate the displayed count from that result.

definition: The organisation of remembered application information into state values and fields. Good structure reduces duplicate data and makes invalid combinations harder to represent.
example: One status string avoids simultaneously setting successful and failed booleans.

definition: Removal of an existing component instance followed by creation of a fresh instance with new local state. A changed key or component type can cause this.
example: Changing a Draft key from recipient 7 to 8 resets the local draft.

definition: The relationship React uses to associate state with a component in the rendered tree, involving its position, component type and key within its parent.
example: A stable task key lets a row retain its state when sibling tasks reorder.

definition: A pure function that calculates next state from current state and an action. It centralises related update rules without mutating inputs or performing external work.
example: A counter reducer handles added and reset action types.

definition: A description of an event supplied to a reducer. By convention it is an object with a type field and any event data needed to calculate next state.
example: { type: "added", amount: 2 } describes an increment event.

definition: The function returned by useReducer that requests a state transition by sending an action. Reading state immediately afterwards still reads the current render’s snapshot.
example: dispatch({ type: "reset" }) asks the reducer to calculate a reset state.

definition: A React Hook that stores state managed by a reducer function and returns the current state plus dispatch. Call it at the top level of a component or custom Hook.
example: useReducer(counterReducer, { count: 0 }) creates a counter state for that component.

definition: A change from one application state to another according to an event and update rule. A reducer makes those rules explicit and testable.
example: An added action moves a counter from count 2 to count 4.

definition: A JavaScript object representing one task in an application, typically with a stable identifier, a title and a completion boolean. It describes application data rather than an asynchronous operation.
example: A task object may contain id 7, title Read, and done false.

definition: A JavaScript object reached through more than one reference. Editing it through any reference changes the same object, so copying a container alone does not protect old state.
example: An array copy can still refer to the same task objects as the original array.

definition: React state whose value is a JavaScript object. Update it by constructing a replacement object rather than changing the existing fields.
example: A profile state object holds a name and an address.

definition: A JavaScript string method that returns a lower-case version of its input string without changing that original string. Lower-casing both a query and task titles supports a simple case-insensitive search.

A JavaScript string method that returns true when one string contains a requested substring, and false otherwise. Matching is case-sensitive unless the strings are transformed first; every string includes an empty string.
A JavaScript array method that rearranges its array in place. Copy a React state array before sorting it, and keep any supplied comparison function free of changes to shared items.
A JavaScript array method that adds items to the end of the existing array. Because it mutates that array, use it only on a fresh local array rather than directly on stored React state.

A JavaScript array method that removes, inserts or replaces items in the existing array. It mutates its receiver, so filter or other replacement calculations are preferable for removing items from React state.
A JavaScript array method that reverses the existing array in place. Make a new array first when reversing React state so the old order remains intact.
A function passed to JavaScript array sort to describe how two items should be ordered. It should consistently compare its inputs without changing them or other shared data.

A JavaScript statement that compares an expression with case values and runs the matching branch. The counter reducer uses action.type to choose a returned state; return exits the function so execution does not continue into later cases.

A JavaScript statement that raises an exception and stops normal execution of the current function. The example reducer throws an error for an unknown action so it cannot silently return an unintended state.
